name: Tool belt
description: A wide leather work belt with two tool pouches, a hammer ring and a row of small tool loops.
notes: Laid flat and straight, outside up: a brown leather strap 1.05 m long and 50 mm wide with a steel buckle at the +x end, two pouches 160 mm by 200 mm with a black front pocket each and screwdriver and plier handles standing out of their tops, a steel hammer ring hanging from a tab between them, and three small loops near the buckle. CHECK VOLUME (x6.3): the reference counts the belt rolled up; laid out flat, its pouches standing open, it spans air. The reference holds seven tools; here two pouches hold small tools and loose parts as grids, the hammer ring is a medium loop point (between the pouches) and the three small loops (near the buckle, front to back) take screwdrivers, pliers or a torch. It has no belt or webbing points: its length is taken by its own pouches. The reference covers the torso; it is the waist item. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Webbing belt
description: A two-inch nylon belt with a row of webbing channels for threading pouches on, and a quick-release steel buckle.
notes: Laid flat and straight, outside up: an olive strap 1.1 m long and 50 mm wide covered in a row of darker webbing channels, a keeper at the tail and a blackened steel quick-release buckle at the +x end. Its six points split the channel row into sixths: the front points are the two sixths either side of the buckle end's middle, the hips the next sixths out, and the back points the two sixths at the tail end. They take the pals standard, since threading pouches through webbing is what the belt is for; gear that only fits belt (the leather belt pouches and quivers) cannot hang on it until a point can accept more than one standard. The reference covers the torso; it is the waist item. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.
